account:
Today I kept my morning appointments and inspected the mill, then returned for council letters. The secretary says no council correspondence arrived. The main unusual matter remains vague talk about changes to the bridge or port, with no definite proposal or official notice that I have seen. My earlier inquiries traced one vague rumour to Townsfolk 03; the innkeeper denied proposing or announcing changes. Today Freight also said people had mentioned changes, but has not identified a source or supplied details. I cannot yet tell whether there is any actual plan behind this talk.

The builder completed the authorized Bridge and Landing Survey and delivered it to the secretary. After a mistaken handover of the Appointments book, which I returned, the secretary brought me the correct report at the cottage. I paid the builder his agreed two emeralds, and the secretary says he acknowledged receipt. The report describes successful bridge passage and a working ferry crossing, with no specific damage observed. It explicitly excludes concealed and underwater structures and nighttime lighting tests; it is not structural safety certification. No repairs or alterations were authorized or performed, and no confirmed defect requiring an estimate was identified. This appears to be an ordinary inspection to establish facts, not evidence of a larger development scheme.

At cottage tea, Freight asked for municipal delivery work and said his warehouse was empty. He asked whether the survey implied landing work, closures, or cargo requirements. I told him there was no authorized delivery or confirmed municipal plan. His questions could simply reflect his wish to find transport business; I have no evidence of another purpose. I asked the neighbour for news but did not hear an intelligible answer. The secretary has been keeping appointment records and handling the survey; the confused book delivery caused delay, but does not by itself establish concealment.

I have now returned to the town hall, late for my 16:30 office appointment. The secretary and builder are nearby, and the baker and innkeeper are outside in the market area. I still want specific names, statements, or documents behind the bridge-and-port rumours rather than treating repeated hearsay as a confirmed plan.
